 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Washington Wizards are on the road Saturday night as they travel to take on the Chicago Bulls in an Eastern Conference matchup.
 Washington enters Saturday's game with a 1-1 record after losing at home to the Toronto Raptors Friday night.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Washington Wizards guard Trae Young (3)Brad Mills-Imagn Images
 In Friday's loss, Trae Young led the way for the Wizards as he recorded 22 points and 12 assists while Bilal Coulibaly added 11 points and six rebounds of his own.
 The Wizards will try to bounce back Saturday as they face off against the Bulls in a tough road matchup.
 Chicago enters Saturday's contest with a 1-1 record after defeating the Milwaukee Bucks on the road Friday afternoon.
 Chicago Bulls guard Norman Powell (24)David Banks-Imagn Images
 Norman Powell led the way for the Bulls in Friday's victory as he ended the game with 25 points and four rebounds while Caleb Wilson recorded 21 points and six rebounds.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While both teams are looking to pick up a victory in Saturday night's matchup, each may be without multiple key players due to injuries.
 Wizards Injury Report: Will AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis Play?
 Washington Wizards forward AJ Dybantsa (4)Stephen Lew-Imagn Images
 The Wizards have three players listed on their injury report , including AJ Dybantsa.
 Washington has ruled out Dybantsa due to a left ankle sprain as he will miss his third consecutive contest.
 The Wizards have also ruled out Tristan Vukcevic due to a left hip impingement and Jamir Watkins is out while recovering from a torn ACL.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Washington Wizards forward Anthony Davis (23)Geoff Burke-Imagn Images
 The good news for the Wizards is that Anthony Davis is not listed on the injury report and will play in the second game of their back-to-back.
 Bulls Injury Report: Will Noa Essengue Play?
 Chicago Bulls forward Noa Essengue (24)David Banks-Imagn Images
 The Bulls have two players listed on their injury report, including forward Noa Essengue.
 Chicago has listed Essengue as probable and he is expected to play despite dealing with a head contusion.
 The Bulls have ruled out Nic Claxton as he remains sidelined with a left hamstring strain.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Fans can catch Saturday night's matchup between the Wizards and Bulls from the United Center at 8 p.m. ET.
